title: Graceful Shutdown & Cleanup Hooks
description: Introduce a built‑in graceful shutdown mechanism that listens for termination signals, stops accepting new connections, waits for in‑flight requests to finish, and runs registered cleanup callbacks. This improves production stability and prevents data loss on container restarts or deployments.
testCases: Simulate SIGTERM while a request is pending; verify the server stops accepting new connections but the pending request completes successfully.
Register a cleanup callback; ensure it is invoked exactly once when the shutdown sequence finishes.
acceptance: When the process receives SIGINT or SIGTERM, the framework stops listening for new requests, waits up to a configurable timeout for active requests to finish, executes all registered cleanup hooks, and then exits with code 0. No new connections are accepted after the signal, and cleanup hooks receive any error thrown during shutdown.
reason: Production deployments frequently need reliable termination to avoid abrupt request drops and resource leaks. Adding graceful shutdown aligns with the recent stability focus and provides a high‑impact, zero‑dependency feature that benefits all users.
